scenes.headline: How a minor update retrained every weight
scenes.sub: Same shapes, new numbers, and what two small boxes can hold.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Hassock! DeepSeek shipped a new Flash model five weeks after the last one. I opened both repos to see what changed.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Config, tokenizer, code and all 96,085 tensor shapes are identical. Every weight shard changed.
scenes.say: The config, the tokenizer, the code and every tensor shape are the same. Only the weights moved, and all of them moved.

steps.say: A prompt only runs through the first twenty layers, the encoder. That keeps prefill to about eight billion active parameters a token.
Two giant n-gram tables feed the encoder. The model hashes the last few tokens and looks rows up instead of multiplying.
The decoder's cache is projected from the encoder's output, just eight hundred and ninety bytes a token.
The decoder reads that cache to write each new token, with six of three hundred and eighty-four experts per layer.

scenes.title: Terminal-Bench 4.0, as the card reports it
scenes.note: the biggest gain, and the row whose agent scaffold changed
scenes.say: Every row on the card went up. The biggest jump is Terminal-Bench, though the new run used a different agent scaffold.

left.title: Opus 5 ahead
left.say: Against Opus five, the new model loses seven rows, including the hardest reasoning exam by a wide margin.

right.title: 1017 ahead
right.say: It wins four, all agentic rows. On par is fair for agent work, and a stretch for the rest.

scenes.title: Cheaper per task, at the same prices

steps.say: DeepSeek's own chart. At max effort the old model cost about forty-nine cents a task. The new one, about twenty cents, and scores higher.

scenes.title: Bytes against two DGX Sparks
scenes.say: As shipped, the model is twice what two Sparks hold. Put the lookup tables on disk, squeeze the experts below three bits, and it fits.

scenes.text: On a Spark, the dense FP8 weights, not the experts, set how fast it decodes.
scenes.say: And here is the surprise. Each token reads more dense weight than expert weight, so squeezing the experts barely speeds up decoding.

recap: Wins agent rows, trails Opus 5 on reasoning
scenes.say: Same model, new weights. Strong on agent work. And two Sparks, only after a re-encode.
